turnaround_reason: EFOR (formerly ASGN, rebranded April 2026) is the #4 US IT staffing firm, beaten down by a soft IT-staffing hiring cycle and weaker federal spending. It stays profitable through the trough and offers a leveraged play on a commercial IT-hiring recovery plus a large federal backlog.
bullish_points: Still profitable through the downturn (trailing P/E 17, forward P/E 7.7, FCF ~$213M) — this is a real cash-generative business, not a broken balance sheet
Very strong insider-buying cluster in Apr 2026: numerous directors and officers bought open-market at $18-22 (now $33) — a broad, high-conviction signal near the bottom
$2.9B federal government contract backlog provides revenue visibility; federal segment tied to data/AI and cybersecurity demand
Recovered above its 200-day MA with positive 5- and 30-day momentum as the base appears to be holding
bearish_points: Stock has already run to $33, above the analyst mean target of $27.50 (recommendation 'hold', 6 analysts) — much of the near-term recovery may be priced in
Fundamentals still deteriorating: Q1 2026 net income -73.7% YoY on flat revenue; TTM revenue growth -1.3%
IT-staffing recovery is being pushed out (analysts cut targets citing softer near-term recovery); AI could also pressure staffing demand
Leverage moderate but present (D/E 83, $1.5B debt); no fresh insider buying since the April cluster
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings showing commercial IT-staffing bookings inflecting and federal backlog conversion accelerating
suggested_trade: Spot only, small; prefer to wait for a pullback toward the mid-$20s (nearer analyst fair value and the insider-buy zone) rather than chase at $33.
key_risk: The IT-staffing recovery keeps slipping and earnings decline further, so a stock already trading above analyst targets re-rates down toward the mid-$20s
would_skip_if: You require an entry with margin of safety — at $33 it trades above fair-value estimates with fundamentals still falling
